method: Fresh rendered web reads. Concise authored paraphrases only; no full publisher pages, dictionary examples, recordings or artwork retained.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: ensure
observations.observation: The current verb concerns making an outcome or condition definite. Its French history is reported as connected to earlier assure forms. That historical relationship alone does not decide a current teaching split.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: en- prefix
observations.observation: The modern prefix has a causative reading used before an adjective base. Its location/condition sense is separately described. This is the prefix entry, not the -en suffix entry.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: sure adjective
observations.section: Result-certainty uses and make sure sense 1
observations.observation: The base expresses certainty, including outcomes certain to occur. The make-sure entry distinguishes bringing about a result from checking a fact; the candidate selects the result reading.

observations.title: Collins dictionaries: ensure
observations.section: Selected outcome sense and American English word history
observations.observation: The whole-word result meaning aligns with the accepted candidate. Word history explicitly links en- with a French predecessor of sure. This corroborates the base boundary while remaining historical evidence.

observations.title: Collins dictionaries: en- prefix
observations.section: British English en- 1 causative sense; American English prefix
observations.observation: Causative use on adjective/noun bases is current. The entry describes productive English formation modeled on French loans and separately distinguishes the Greek in/within prefix and -en suffix.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: inform
observations.section: Recipient-information sense, verb forms and Word Origin
observations.observation: Current giving-information and influence meanings are separate. The forms include informed and informing. Historical development concerns shaping or forming the mind, through an into-prefix and form/shape base; it is not negative in- or a document-form meaning.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: informed adjective
observations.section: Knowledgeable person/state and decision based on understanding
observations.observation: The adjective includes having knowledge and a decision grounded in understanding. This supports a plausible family relation to inform while showing why having been told something alone does not settle an informed decision or clinical consent.

observations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: collect verb
observations.section: Bring-together sense, distinct take-away sense, verb forms and Word Origin
observations.observation: The selected sense brings items together from several sources; pickup is separate. Forms retain collect before inflections. The historical chain passes through Latin collect- and colligere, with together and gather/choose elements.

observations.title: Collins dictionaries: collect
observations.section: Selected gathering sense, verb forms and verb word history
observations.observation: Gathering from several people/places is distinct from pickup and payment meanings. Historical analysis describes Latin col-/com-, legere and participial development. The prayer noun and unrelated senses are excluded from the proposal.

excluded_retrievals.observation: The retrieved page is the -en suffix, not the intended prefix. It is excluded as proof for the ensure prefix; the correct en_1 page was then inspected.
Current gathering meanings were visible, but the tool's History and Etymology search returned no matching text. No historical inference is drawn from this retrieval.

limits: Dictionary meanings, forms, productive-prefix descriptions and histories support a research proposal, not a complete formal morphological analysis or evidence that a learning exercise works. No source CEFR label is reinterpreted as morphology difficulty or approval.
